scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Relief in Case of Death or Disability of Registered Building Workers
description:
The Scheme to Provide Relief in Case of Death or Disability of Registered Building Workers was launched by the Government of India to support the welfare of construction workers. 

This scheme was introduced in the year 2006 under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the families of registered building workers in the event of death or disability. 

The scheme aims to ensure that the families of deceased or disabled workers do not face financial hardships during difficult times. 

The scheme provides a monetary relief of ₹2 lakh in case of death of a registered building worker. 

In the case of permanent disability, the scheme offers a financial assistance of ₹1 lakh. 

This financial assistance is aimed at helping families cope with sudden loss of income due to the death or disability of the breadwinner. 

To be eligible for this scheme, an individual must be a registered building worker. 

The registration of building workers is conducted through the respective state welfare boards. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years of age to qualify for registration as building workers. 

There is no upper age limit for registration. 

The income criteria for eligibility is set at a maximum of ₹15,000 per month. 

Workers must provide proof of their employment in the construction sector to be eligible for registration. 

The application process for this scheme involves several steps. 

First, the applicant must obtain a registration form from the respective state building and other construction workers' welfare board. 

The form can also be downloaded from the official websites of these boards. 

Next, the applicant must fill out the form with accurate personal details and employment information. 

The applicant is required to submit documents such as proof of identity, proof of residence, and proof of employment. 

Once the form is completed, it must be submitted to the local office of the state welfare board. 

The application will be verified by the officials of the welfare board. 

Upon successful verification, the applicant will be registered as a building worker. 

In the event of death or disability, the family or the worker must apply for the relief. 

The application for relief must be submitted along with the death certificate or disability certificate. 

The family must also provide proof of registration of the deceased or disabled worker. 

The relief amount is typically disbursed within 30 days of the application being approved. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Labour and Employment at the central level. 

At the state level, the respective State Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Boards are responsible for implementation. 

These boards are tasked with the registration of workers and the disbursement of benefits under the scheme. 

The scheme is part of a larger initiative to improve the welfare of workers in the unorganized sector. 

As of 2023, over 50 lakh workers have been registered under this scheme across various states. 

The scheme has seen an increase in awareness and participation since its inception. 

The government has also launched awareness campaigns to inform workers about their rights and benefits under this scheme. 

Workers are encouraged to register to ensure that they and their families are protected in case of unforeseen circumstances. 

The scheme is funded by the Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Cess Act, 1996. 

The cess is collected at the rate of 1% of the cost of construction incurred by employers. 

This fund is utilized for the welfare of construction workers, including the relief scheme. 

The scheme also aims to reduce the financial burden on families during tragic events. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme promotes social security for construction workers. 

The government is continuously monitoring the implementation of the scheme to ensure timely disbursement of benefits. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme and address any issues faced by workers. 

The scheme is part of the broader vision of the Indian government to provide social security to all workers. 

The government has set a target to increase the registration of building workers by 20% annually. 

This initiative is crucial as the construction sector is one of the largest employers in India. 

The scheme also contributes to the overall development of the construction industry by ensuring worker welfare. 

The government aims to create a more secure environment for workers in the construction sector. 

The scheme has been instrumental in providing immediate financial support to families in distress. 

It has been reported that the scheme has significantly reduced the economic impact of sudden loss of income on families. 

The relief provided under this scheme is a critical lifeline for many families across the country. 

The government continues to explore ways to enhance the benefits offered under this scheme. 

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the scheme. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to worker welfare and social security. 

In conclusion, the Scheme to Provide Relief in Case of Death or Disability of Registered Building Workers is a vital initiative aimed at protecting the livelihoods of construction workers and their families. 

With specific financial assistance amounts and a clear application process, it provides essential support during times of need. 

The eligibility criteria ensure that those who are genuinely in need can access the benefits. 

The implementation by state welfare boards ensures localized support for workers across India. 

This scheme reflects the government's ongoing efforts to improve the welfare of workers in the unorganized sector.
